subject: In-region processing assurance and SCCs: operational carve-outs Q&A
messages:
From: Claire Pflug <claire.pflug@jurassicpharma.eu>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-03-11T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: EU-only processing, SCCs and retention clarifications

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this early. We are finalizing our vendor assessment for a pilot using Redwood for inference on patient-derived data. Before we proceed to procurement we need clear answers on a few operational points tied to Schrems II / SCCs compliance and our internal retention policies:

- Can you confirm whether both inference compute and the control plane can be restricted to within the EU (primary region DE-FRA)?
- How are backups handled: are snapshots kept outside the region, what is the retention window for backups, and how quickly can those be purged on customer request?
- Operator/engineer access: what are the conditions for Redwood staff to access customer data or logs (on-call, emergency, legal process)? Are access events logged and auditable?
- KMS: is there an option for customer-managed keys (BYOK) that remain in-region?
- Evidence: we will need an attestation or artifact bundle (SCCs mapping, operator access policy, deletion evidence examples) for our legal team.

Can you provide the above or point me to the relevant artifacts? If helpful we can schedule a 30-minute sync with our security and legal folks.

Best,
Claire Pflug
Head of Procurement
Jurassic Pharma GmbH
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Pflug <claire.pflug@jurassicpharma.eu>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-03-11T11:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing, SCCs and retention clarifications

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a proposed next step:

1) EU-only processing: Yes — for our EU Dedicated / Private customers we can pin inference compute and the control plane to an EU region (we normally use DE-FRA for EU-only commitments).

2) Backups & retention: Snapshots are stored encrypted in-region by default. Retention is configurable; standard retention is 90 days but we can shorten that contractually for customers who require shorter windows. Purge processes are initiated within 72 hours and we provide a signed confirmation when completed.

3) Operator access: Access is strictly role-based. Production operator access to customer workloads is limited to a small SRE roster under NDA and only granted for defined maintenance or incident scenarios. All access is logged, IAM-authorized, and reviewed; logs are retained and can be included in an evidence bundle.

4) KMS/BYOK: We support customer-managed keys via supported KMS providers (customer retains key ownership). Key material remains under customer control and, in the case of BYOK, KMS location can be constrained to the EU.

5) Evidence: I attached a short summary (eu-processing-summary.pdf) and Ben will follow up with the SCCs-subprocessor mapping workbook. We can also provide a time-stamped attestation and a sample deletion certificate for customers who require it.

If helpful, let's schedule a 30-minute call with your security and legal teams this week — are you available Thu 13th 10:00–10:30 CET?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: eu-processing-summary.pdf (1 page summary — in-region architecture, retention options, operator controls)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Pflug <claire.pflug@jurassicpharma.eu>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-03-11T13:28:00+01:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing, SCCs and retention clarifications

On Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 11:03 Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 2) Backups & retention: Snapshots are stored encrypted in-region by default...

Claire — quick technical follow-up and clarifications from the infra side: 

- Backups: snapshots are encrypted at rest with AES-256 and stored in the configured EU region. We run incremental snapshots; full-snapshot deletion is coordinated via a purge job and the object lifecycle rule removes remaining fragments. For contractual short-retention customers we can configure lifecycle to 30 days.
- Deletion proof: we produce an audit snapshot showing object deletion timestamps, snapshot IDs, and worker logs. For legal teams we can provide a signed attestation plus a sanitized export of the deletion log (redacted where required).
- Operator access & emergency flow: operator Access Requests are granted via short-lived certificates with just-in-time elevation and are captured in our central audit log (who/why/when). In cases of lawful process (e.g., court order) we route through our legal team and notify the customer per contract.
- SCCs mapping: the attached sccs-operator-mapping.xlsx maps subprocessors to SCC appendices and the locations where data may be processed. Note: where a third-party subprocessor must perform maintenance we try to limit data exposure (pseudonymization + ephemeral access).

Happy to go deeper on any of the above on the call.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sccs-operator-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet mapping subprocessors and SCC references)
